title: Paneer-Stuffed Kulcha with Garlic-Coriander Ghee
summary: Soft, pillowy flatbread stuffed with spiced paneer and onion, pan-cooked until blistered and brushed with garlicky ghee.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
warm water, plus more as needed
coriander leaves and stems, finely chopped
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine 300 g plain flour, 2 tsp instant yeast, 1 tsp sugar and 1 tsp fine salt, add 28 g yoghurt, 1 tbsp oil and most of the 170 ml warm water, then knead to a soft dough, 5-7 min.

steps.title: Prove
steps.text: Cover and leave the dough until doubled, 60-75 min.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Mix 150 g grated paneer with 70 g onion, 2 tbsp coriander, 2 chillies, 1 tsp ginger, ½ tsp garlic, ½ tsp cumin, ½ tsp ground coriander, ½ tsp amchur, ½ tsp chilli powder and ¼ tsp salt.

steps.title: Stuff
steps.text: Divide the dough into 8 balls, flatten each to a 10 cm disc, spoon in the filling and gather the edges to seal.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Press each stuffed ball flat, seam side down, and roll gently to about 15 cm.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Fry in a dry pan over medium-high heat until puffed with brown spots, 1-2 min per side.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Brush with a mix of 2 tbsp melted ghee and 1 grated garlic clove, then scatter with chopped coriander and ½ tsp nigella seeds.

tips: Keep unrolled dough balls covered so they don't dry out while you work through the batch.
Roll gently rather than firmly so the filling stays inside instead of bursting through.
Wrap cooked kulcha in a tea towel to keep them soft and warm until serving.
storage: Serve warm on the day of making; wrap any extras in a tea towel to keep them soft or reheat briefly in a hot pan. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
